name: Nabla vs Suki AI
title: Nabla vs Suki AI: Ambient AI Scribe Comparison 2026
description: Compare Nabla and Suki AI ambient medical scribes. See pricing, EHR integrations, language support, and features to choose the best AI documentation solution.

summary.bottom_line: Nabla excels in multilingual support (35+ languages) and privacy (zero data storage on servers), making it ideal for diverse patient populations and telehealth. Suki AI offers deeper EHR integration with voice commands beyond documentation, making it better for health systems wanting hands-free chart navigation alongside ambient documentation.

sections.heading: Nabla vs Suki AI: Overview
sections.content: Nabla and Suki AI are both leading ambient AI documentation platforms, but they serve different primary use cases. Nabla, founded in Paris in 2018, emphasizes privacy (patient data never stored on servers) and multilingual support (35+ languages) - ideal for telehealth and diverse populations. Suki AI, founded by ex-Google product manager Punit Soni, goes beyond documentation with voice commands for EHR navigation, ordering, and clinical Q&A - making it a full clinical assistant. Suki has raised significantly more funding ($168M vs $24M) and has deeper enterprise EHR integrations.

sections.heading: Pricing Comparison
sections.content: Both platforms are premium-priced. Nabla historically charged ~$119/month for individual plans with enterprise pricing at $299-399/provider/month. Suki AI starts at $299/month for Suki Compose (documentation) and $399/month for Suki Assistant (full EHR commands). Both require quotes for enterprise deployments. Neither publishes current pricing publicly - sales conversations are required.

sections.heading: Key Capability Differences
sections.content: The fundamental difference is scope: Nabla focuses on ambient documentation with industry-leading privacy (data only exists in the clinician's browser) and multilingual support. Suki AI extends beyond documentation to voice-activated EHR commands for hands-free chart navigation, ordering, and clinical queries. If you only need documentation, Nabla's privacy model may be preferable. If you want a full voice-controlled clinical assistant, Suki's broader capabilities justify its higher price.

sections.heading: EHR Integration & Compliance
sections.content: Suki has deeper EHR integrations with bi-directional, real-time connectivity to Epic, Cerner, athenahealth, and MEDITECH Expanse - essential for voice commands. Nabla uses SMART on FHIR and its Nabla Connect platform to embed in 20+ EHRs. Suki is HITRUST certified while Nabla is SOC 2 and GDPR compliant. For European practices or those prioritizing GDPR, Nabla may be preferable.

sections.heading: Which Should You Choose?
sections.content: Choose based on your primary needs:

recommendations.when: You prioritize data privacy (zero server storage), serve diverse populations needing multilingual support (35+ languages), or are GDPR-conscious
You want a full clinical assistant with voice commands for EHR navigation and ordering, not just documentation
You're a telehealth provider or have patients who speak multiple languages and need documentation in those languages
You use Epic, Cerner, athena, or MEDITECH and want the deepest possible bi-directional integration for hands-free workflows

faqs.q: Which has better language support: Nabla or Suki AI?
faqs.a: Suki AI supports 80+ languages for transcription, while Nabla supports 35+ languages. However, Nabla emphasizes multilingual documentation as a core feature, while Suki's strength is more in English-language EHR voice commands.

faqs.q: Does Nabla store patient data on its servers?
faqs.a: No, Nabla's privacy model means patient audio, transcripts, and notes exist only in the clinician's browser and are never stored on Nabla's servers. This is a unique privacy advantage among AI scribes.

faqs.q: Can Suki AI control my EHR with voice commands?
faqs.a: Yes, Suki AI goes beyond documentation to offer voice commands for EHR navigation, ordering, charting, and clinical Q&A. This makes it a clinical assistant, not just an AI scribe.

faqs.q: Which is cheaper: Nabla or Suki AI?
faqs.a: Nabla is generally cheaper, with individual plans historically around $119/month compared to Suki's $299-399/month. However, both require custom quotes for current pricing.
